title: The additive two-way model
html:
Assume @eq-tw-additive with m≥1 observations in every cell.

  1. P0,PA,PB and R are mutually orthogonal projections summing to I, with ranks 1, a−1, b−1 and n−a−b+1. The projection onto C(X) is M=P0+PA+PB, and the fitted values are y^ijk=y¯i⋅⋅+y¯⋅j⋅−y¯⋅⋅⋅.

  2. λ0μ+∑iλiαi+∑jκjβj is estimable iff λ0=∑iλi=∑jκj. The BLUE of a contrast ∑iciαi is ∑iciy¯i⋅⋅, with variance σ2∑ici2/(bm). These are the estimate and variance of the one-way layout in A that ignores B. The estimate of a contrast in the αi is uncorrelated with the estimate of any contrast in the βj.

  3. Under normal errors, SSA=‖PAy‖2=bm∑i(y¯i⋅⋅−y¯⋅⋅⋅)2, SSB=‖PBy‖2=am∑j(y¯⋅j⋅−y¯⋅⋅⋅)2 and SSE=‖Ry‖2 are independent, SSE/σ2∼χ2(n−a−b+1), and FA=SSA/(a−1)SSE/(n−a−b+1)∼F(a−1, n−a−b+1, γA),γA=bmσ2∑i(αi−α¯)2, with α¯=a−1∑iαi. So FA is an exact test of α1=⋯=αa. Its numerator is that of the one-way F test in A that ignores B (@thm-aov-oneway-f); only the error term differs. The same holds for B, with γB=(am/σ2)∑j(βj−β¯)2.

  4. If m≥2, then R=PAB+PE with PAB=Ca⊗Cb⊗J¯m and PE=Ia⊗Ib⊗Cm, of ranks (a−1)(b−1) and ab(m−1). The squared lengths ‖PABy‖2 and ‖PEy‖2 are the lack-of-fit and pure-error sums of squares of the additive model (@def-cor-pure-error). If the cell means μij are arbitrary, the lack-of-fit F test of additivity has noncentrality γAB=mσ2∑i,j(μij−μ¯i⋅−μ¯⋅j+μ¯⋅⋅)2.

  5. If m=1, then R=Ca⊗Cb, and the residual space consists of the a×b tables whose rows and columns all sum to zero. There is no pure error.

  6. (Tukey’s test.) If m=1, the errors are normal and (a−1)(b−1)≥2, then with SSN as in @eq-tw-tukey-ss, FN=SSN(SSE−SSN)/((a−1)(b−1)−1)∼F(1, (a−1)(b−1)−1).
